items.title: Japan PM protests to US after Marine arrested on murder suspicion in Okinawa
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi registered a protest with the United States on Sunday after a US Marine was arrested on suspicion of robbing and murdering a Japanese woman in Okinawa.
items.body:
Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi registered a protest with the United States on Sunday after a US Marine was arrested on suspicion of robbing and murdering a Japanese woman in Okinawa.
Devin Jacob Ballard, 20, is suspected of killing Anna Yagi, 39, in a hotel in Naha, the capital of the southernmost prefecture, on Saturday and taking her wallet and backpack, police said. Ballard denied the allegations, police said.
"The occurrence of such an extremely brutal and vicious incident is extremely regrettable," Takaichi said in a statement.
"The government of Japan strongly protests to the US side and strongly seeks maximum cooperation with the investigation," as well as the tightening of discipline and thorough measures to prevent a recurrence, she said.
The US embassy and the Marine Corps expressed condolences over the incident and said they were cooperating with the Japanese authorities.
The Marines said in a statement that the suspect, who is assigned to the III Marine Expeditionary Force and based at Marine Corps Air Station Futenma, was in Japanese custody.
"The Marine Corps takes these allegations very seriously and expects every Marine to adhere to the highest standards of behavior," it said.
Most of the 18,000 Japan-based Marines are stationed in Okinawa, which the US held from the end of World War Two until 1972. Their presence has repeatedly stirred resentment among residents over issues such as noise, aircraft crashes and the conduct of personnel.
The 1995 rape of a 12-year-old Okinawan girl by three US servicemen sparked mass protests.
Saturday's killing could complicate Takaichi's efforts to [USN:L1N455098 TEXT:"relocate some Marines"] from the busy Futenma air base to a more remote facility at Henoko. Opponents want the troops moved out of the prefecture.
Okinawa, which is 100 km (60 miles) from Taiwan at the closest point, is viewed by Tokyo and Washington as key in deterring potential military aggression from China.

items.title: Kirill Kaprizov, Wild overcome slow start to blow past Bruins
items.author: Field Level Media
items.creator: Field Level Media
items.summary: Kirill Kaprizov scored a pair of goals, and the Minnesota Wild pulled away for a 4-1 win over the Boston Bruins on Saturday night in Saint Paul, Minn.
items.body:
Kirill Kaprizov scored a pair of goals, and the Minnesota Wild pulled away for a 4-1 win over the Boston Bruins on Saturday night in Saint Paul, Minn.
Quinn Hughes tallied a goal and an assist for Minnesota, which won its second game in a row to start the season. Wild captain Jared Spurgeon also scored a goal.
Tanner Jeannot scored the lone goal for Boston, which was playing on short rest after defeating the Winnipeg Jets one night earlier.
Wild goaltender Jesper Wallstedt stopped 26 of 27 shots to earn the victory.
Bruins goaltender Michael DiPietro allowed three goals on 29 shots in his season debut. DiPietro stuffed Wild forward Matt Boldy on a breakaway but allowed a pair of power-play goals.
The Bruins opened the scoring less than two minutes into the game. Jeannot set up toward the left side of the crease, took a short pass from Mark Kastelic and fired the puck into the back of the net for his first goal of the season.
Boston held that lead for over a full period before Minnesota pulled even with 13:49 to go in the second period. The Wild capitalized on a power-play opportunity when Maxim Shabanov got the puck behind the net and passed it to Kaprizov, who scored on a snap shot.
The Wild delivered on the power play once again to grab a 2-1 lead with 7:32 remaining in the second period. Ryan Hartman won a faceoff and Bobby Brink redirected the puck to Hughes, who skated to the high slot and unleashed a wrist shot through traffic that beat DiPietro.
Minnesota made it 3-1 with 16:36 left in the third period. Spurgeon fired a long shot that deflected off the skate of Bruins defender Nikita Zadorov and into the net.
Kaprizov capped the scoring when he punched in a backhanded shot for an empty-net goal with 1:01 to go. The play gave him three goals in two games to start the season.
-Field Level Media

items.title: テニス＝ルバキナ、世界ランク1位としての初戦で逆転負け
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［３日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
［３日　ロイター］ - テニスの中国オープン（ＯＰ）は３日、北京で試合を行い、女子シングルス２回戦で世界ランキング１位のエレーナ・ルバキナ（カザフスタン）が初戦敗退を喫した。

この日が初戦となった第１シードのルバキナは、アリーナ・チャラエワ（アルメニア）と対戦し、第１セットは６─３で奪ったものの、続くセットを４─６、３─６で落として逆転負け。９月の全米ＯＰで優勝し、キャリア初の世界ランク１位となったルバキナだが、トップに浮上した後の最初の試合で敗れた選手としては、大坂なおみに次ぐ史上２人目となった。

ＷＴＡランキングは１９７５年に初めて発表されたが、ＯｐｔａＡｃｅによると、それ以降で世界ランク１位の相手に逆転勝ちを収めた選手では、今回のチャラエワ（１１８位）が最もランクの低いプレーヤーだという。

ルバキナは「間違いなく、今日は非常に厳しい試合だった。全米ＯＰで優勝してからいろいろなことがあった。睡眠や回復の機会をあまり持てなかった。アリーナをお祝いしたい。彼女は素晴らしい試合をした」と話した。

items.title: ＮＢＡ＝ピストンズ、デューレンとの契約延長を正式に発表
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［３日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
［３日　ロイター］ - 米プロバスケットボール協会（ＮＢＡ）のピストンズが３日、制限付きフリーエージェント（ＦＡ）のセンター、ジェイレン・デューレン（２２）との契約延長を正式に発表した。

これまで米スポーツ専門チャンネルＥＳＰＮとジ・アスレチックは５年総額２億ドル（約３１６億円）と報じていたが、チームは契約の詳細を明かしていない。

ピストンズのバスケットボール運営部門代表を務めるトラジャン・ラングドン氏は「今後何年もジェイレンをチームの中心に据えられることをうれしく思う」とし、「彼は若くして多くを成し遂げており、われわれは彼の全盛期はこれからだと信じている」と述べた。

報道によると、ピストンズは最近デューレンに同じ総額２億ドルの契約を提示したものの、体重に関する条項を盛り込んでいたという。今回の合意では同条項が削除されたと報じられている。

昨季初めてオールスターとオールＮＢＡに選出されたデューレンは、レギュラーシーズンで自己最多の１試合平均１９．５得点に加え、１０．５リバウンドを記録。ピストンズは６０勝２２敗で東カンファレンス最高成績を残した。一方、プレーオフでは同１０．２得点、８．５リバウンドに数字を落とし、チームは東カンファレンス準決勝でキャバリアーズに３勝４敗で敗れた。

items.title: First-period goals hold up as Predators fend off Stars
items.author: Field Level Media
items.creator: Field Level Media
items.summary: First-period goals by Steven Stamkos and Nils Hoglander held up to the final buzzer as the host Nashville Predators claimed a 2-1 victory over the Dallas Stars on Saturday for their first win of the season.
items.body:
First-period goals by Steven Stamkos and Nils Hoglander held up to the final buzzer as the host Nashville Predators claimed a 2-1 victory over the Dallas Stars on Saturday for their first win of the season.
Goaltender Juuse Saros made 29 saves -- 12 in the third period -- for the Predators, who rebounded after opening the campaign with a home loss to the Minnesota Wild on Thursday.
Miro Heiskanen scored for the Stars, who have dropped two consecutive games to begin the season.
Goalie Casey DeSmith stopped 24 shots and was denied the 100th victory of his career.
With his team trailing after an early Dallas goal, Stamkos tied it on the power play when he unloaded a one-timer from the left faceoff dot set up by Ryan O'Reilly for the 625th goal of his career.
Stamkos is tied with a pair of Hall of Fame luminaries in Joe Sakic -- one of his boyhood idols -- and Jarome Iginla for 17th on the NHL's all-time goals list.
O'Reilly's assist was the 899th point of his career.
The Predators carried the momentum and took the lead when Hoglander netted his first of the season by redirecting the point shot for another man-advantage tally at 15:49.
Dallas regained its footing and pushed the rest of the way, but Saros held strong.
Coming off a season-opening 4-0 loss to the visiting St. Louis Blues on Friday, the Stars were looking for a quick start and received it when Heiskanen opened the scoring 47 seconds into the clash by finishing a scramble.
Nashville defenseman William Trudeau, claimed off waivers from the New York Rangers late last month, made his NHL debut.
--Field Level Media

items.title: Penguins relinquish 4-goal lead, recover to beat Canadiens in OT
items.author: Field Level Media
items.creator: Field Level Media
items.summary: Tommy Novak scored two goals, including the game-winner at 1:33 of overtime, and also had an assist to give the Pittsburgh Penguins a wild 6-5 victory over the visiting Montreal Canadiens on Saturday night.
items.body:
Tommy Novak scored two goals, including the game-winner at 1:33 of overtime, and also had an assist to give the Pittsburgh Penguins a wild 6-5 victory over the visiting Montreal Canadiens on Saturday night.
Evgeni Malkin, who finished with a goal and two assists, crossed a pass past Montreal defenseman Mike Matheson to Novak at the bottom of the right circle on a 2-on-1 break and Novak roofed a wrist shot over goaltender Jakub Dobes for the game-winner.
Erik Karlsson and Kris Letang each had two assists and Ben Kindel, Declan Carlile and Samuel Girard also scored goals for Pittsburgh, which won despite blowing a 5-1 lead. Arturs Silovs made 20 saves.
Sidney Crosby had an assist, the 1,109th of his career, moving him into a tie with Joe Thornton for seventh in NHL history.
Nick Suzuki had a goal and three assists, Cole Caufield scored two goals, Chris Kreider and Ivan Demidov each had a goal and an assist and Lane Hutson chipped in with three assists for Montreal. Dobes finished with 24 saves.
Montreal, which opened the season with a 3-2 victory at Toronto, jumped out to a 1-0 lead at the 3:49 mark of the first period when Caufield snapped a wrist shot from the right circle inside the far left post.
Pittsburgh tied it on a power-play goal by Malkin, who chipped in a rebound of a Kris Letang shot for his second goal of the season..
The Penguins then scored four consecutive goals to start the second period to take a 5-1 lead. Carlile started the blitz 32 seconds into the period with a wrist shot from the top of the right circle that beat Dobes on his glove side. Girard followed when he roofed a backhand pass from Crosby from the low slot. Novak then finished a 2-on-1 rush with a wrist shot off an Egor Chinakov cross, and Kindel made it 5-1 with a power-play goal, redirecting a point shot by Karlsson into the top right corner of the net.
Suzuki cut the lead to 5-2 just before the end of the period when he split a pair of defenders and fired a shot over Silovs' right shoulder. Caufield got his second goal of the game early in the third period with a wrist shot from the high slot to close the gap to two.
The Canadiens then scored twice in the final 68 seconds to earn a point and force overtime, the first by Kreider and the second by Demidov off a Suzuki crossing pass with 44 seconds to go.
--Field Level Media

items.title: Argentina golea 7-0 a Burkina Faso en partido amistoso
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: La selección de fútbol de Argentina exhibió el sábado su renovado poderío ofensivo, sin la presencia de Lionel Messi, al golear por 7-0 a Burkina Faso en un partido amistoso en el marco de la fecha FIFA.
items.body:
La selección de fútbol de Argentina exhibió el sábado su renovado poderío ofensivo, sin la presencia de Lionel Messi, al golear por 7-0 a Burkina Faso en un partido amistoso en el marco de la fecha FIFA.
Los goles del triunfo los anotaron Lautaro Martínez, Gianluca Prestiani, Nicolás Paz, Julián Álvarez, Giovani Simeone, Franco Mastantuono y Moumouni Daillo en contra de su propia valla.
Argentina fue muy superior al joven seleccionado africano que arribó a Buenos Aires pocas horas antes del inicio del partido luego de afrontar dificultades logísticas con el viaje, de acuerdo a un comunicado de la organización.
La "albiceleste" volverá a jugar el martes ante Benín en el estadio Monumental, en un partido con el que Messi se despedirá de la selección.
El astro, que capitaneó a Argentina hacia la victoria en la Copa del Mundo de 2022 y la final de 2026, comunicó un mes atrás su retiro del equipo nacional luego de 19 años, pero sigue su carrera en Inter Miami.
"Sabemos que se nos va Leo y ahora empieza todo un camino nuevo con chicos que se suman. Hay un gran grupo que se formó y seguiremos con la misma línea", dijo Enzo Fernández tras la goleada.
En el partido disputado en el estadio Monumental, Argentina aprovechó una infracción innecesaria dentro del área para abrir el marcador a los cuatro minutos a través de Lautaro Martínez, al convertir en el rebote de un penal que le tapó el portero Razak Guira.
Cuatro minutos después, otro error de Burkina Faso le permitió al conjunto dirigido por Lionel Scaloni ampliar la ventaja gracias a un gol de Moumouni Daillo en contra de su propia puerta tras un remate de Julián Álvarez.
Antes del final de la primera parte, la "Albiceleste" anotó otros tres goles por intermedio de Gianluca Prestiani, Nicolás Paz y Julián Álvarez a los 24, 34 y 36 minutos, respectivamente.
En el segundo tiempo, Argentina completó la goleada con tantos de Franco Mastantuono y Giuliano Simeone a los minutos 77 y 92.
"Estoy muy contento de volverme a poner la camiseta de Argentina. Me quedé afuera del Mundial y fue triste, pero tenía que seguir trabajando para volver y hoy me tocó hacer un gol", dijo Mastantuono.

items.title: Islanders rout Devils in home-opening shutout
items.author: Field Level Media
items.creator: Field Level Media
items.summary: Simon Holmstrom, Brayden Schenn and Bo Horvat scored within a nine-minute span in the second period Saturday night and goalie Ilya Sorokin stopped all 37 shots he faced for the New York Islanders, who won their home opener by routing the New Jersey Devils 6-0.
items.body:
Simon Holmstrom, Brayden Schenn and Bo Horvat scored within a nine-minute span in the second period Saturday night and goalie Ilya Sorokin stopped all 37 shots he faced for the New York Islanders, who won their home opener by routing the New Jersey Devils 6-0.
Victor Eklund, Ondrej Palat and Casey Cizikas scored in the third for the Islanders, who bounced back from a 2-1 season-opening loss at Toronto. Reigning Calder Trophy winner Matthew Schaefer had two assists.
The shutout for Sorokin was the franchise-record 30th of his career.
Nico Daws made 26 saves for the Devils, who have also split their first two games.
The Devils outshot the Islanders 9-7 in a scoreless first before the hosts took control into the second.
Adam Pelech set up Holmstrom's goal by weaving through the neutral zone and dishing to Jean-Gabriel Pageau, who drew Daws to the right of the crease before dishing to Holmstrom. The winger then sent a shot over the right leg of the sprawling Daws at 3:32.
A Devils turnover led to Schenn's goal just 88 seconds later. Schaefer picked off Stefan Noesen's pass just in front of the blue line and fired a shot that bounced off Daws. Eklund picked up the puck and sent a pass between his and Daws' legs to Schenn, who buried the point-blank chance.
Schaefer collected another assist with 7:52 left in the second, when he fed Horvat at the front of the right faceoff circle before the Islanders captain directed a shot beyond Daws' glove.
Eklund celebrated his 20th birthday by scoring his first NHL goal with 8:28 left in the third, when he got a stick on Calum Ritchie's pass and tucked a shot over Daws' glove. Palat added another insurance goal just 42 seconds later and Cizikas, in his 16th season with the Islanders, scored a short-handed goal with 1:19 left.
--Field Level Media

items.title: Canes rally past Flyers in OT to secure first win of title defense
items.author: Field Level Media
items.creator: Field Level Media
items.summary: Shayne Gostisbehere scored a power-play goal in overtime to lift the Carolina Hurricanes to their first victory of the season with a 3-2 road win over the Philadelphia Flyers on Saturday.
items.body:
Shayne Gostisbehere scored a power-play goal in overtime to lift the Carolina Hurricanes to their first victory of the season with a 3-2 road win over the Philadelphia Flyers on Saturday.
Gostisbehere's decisive goal was a one-timer from the top of the left circle at 2:51 of the extra session. The former Flyers defenseman benefited from a terrific screen from Andrei Svechnikov, who knocked down Philadelphia's Nick Seeler before impeding Joseph Woll's vision in front of the net.
Pyotr Kochetkov made 16 saves to earn the win for Carolina, which had lost its first two contests of the young campaign. The defending champions' first two goals Saturday came courtesy of Sebastian Aho, including one 10 seconds into the contest.
Owen Tippett and Matvei Michkov scored for Philadelphia, which was swept by Carolina in the Eastern Conference semifinals last season. Woll turned aside 37 shots for the hosts, who remain winless in three games this season.
The game could not have gotten off to a better start for the Hurricanes, who promptly scored off the opening faceoff. William Carrier quickly centered the puck right past Flyers center Christian Dvorak and onto the stick of Aho, who snapped one past Woll.
Philadelphia drew even at 8:03 of the first period as Tippett collected a loose puck in the high slot and buried a shot past Kochetkov.
Michkov's first of the season gave the Flyers a 2-1 lead at 7:20 of the second period.
However, Aho tied it at 2-2 early in the third period, as he scored a power-play goal from a similar spot to his first tally. This one came off a feed from Nikolaj Ehlers, setting up Aho's one-timer.
The Flyers went on the power play late in regulation, but they struggled to enter the offensive zone. The man advantage carried over into overtime, when Tyson Foerster and Trevor Zegras had quality scoring chances, although Kochetkov held firm.
Shortly thereafter, Carolina received a power play of its own when Tippett was whistled for slashing. With the Hurricanes skating 4-on-3, Svechnikov's one-timer was denied by Woll. However, Gostisbehere buried the game-winner less than a minute later.
Philadelphia defenseman Rasmus Ristolainen left with an apparent hand injury. The team said he'll be further evaluated Sunday.
--Field Level Media

items.title: Senators break tie in third, edge Leafs in season opener
items.author: Field Level Media
items.creator: Field Level Media
items.summary: Stephen Halliday scored the tiebreaking goal midway through the third period Saturday night and the visiting Ottawa Senators won their season opener, defeating the host Toronto Maple Leafs 3-2.
items.body:
Stephen Halliday scored the tiebreaking goal midway through the third period Saturday night and the visiting Ottawa Senators won their season opener, defeating the host Toronto Maple Leafs 3-2.
Newly appointed captain Thomas Chabot had a goal and assist and Michael Amadio also scored for Ottawa. Claude Giroux added two assists and Linus Ullmark stopped 27 shots.
Auston Matthews and Kirill Marchenko scored for the Maple Leafs, who have lost two of their first three games, all at home.
Sergei Bobrovsky made 26 saves for the Maple Leafs.
The Maple Leafs hit both posts with shots in the first period. Teddy Blueger hit the left post at 13:28 on a redirect. Jack Roslovic hit the right post at 13:58.
Ottawa scored the first goal when Chabot jumped up on the rush and knocked in a 12-footer off a rebound at 18:51 of the first period.
Toronto tied the game 33 seconds into the second period on a tip-in by Matthews on Morgan Rielly's shot from the point.
Marchenko flipped in a backhand shot on a pass from Darren Raddysh at 7:06 of the second on a power play. Giroux was off for slashing.
Amadio tied the game at 12:40 of the second on a 2-on-1 counter with Tim Stutzle, who made a deft pass to the edge of the crease. Toronto had just been foiled on a rush.
Halliday snapped in a five-footer at 9:46 of the third on a rebound to give Ottawa the lead.
Toronto had a power-play chance at 14:20 of the third but did not get a shot on goal.
Bobrovsky was pulled for an extra attacker with just under three minutes left in regulation. Matthews hit the post at 18:08. Bobrovsky had to return to the net after the Senators applied pressure.
Ottawa defenseman Jake Sanderson did not return after the first period due to an undisclosed injury.
--Field Level Media

items.title: Andrei Vasilevskiy sharp as Lightning beat Capitals
items.author: Field Level Media
items.creator: Field Level Media
items.summary: Reigning Vezina Trophy winner Andrei Vasilevskiy stopped 20 shots in his 600th career game, and the Tampa Bay Lightning won for the first time this season by topping the visiting Washington Capitals 3-1 on Saturday night.
items.body:
Reigning Vezina Trophy winner Andrei Vasilevskiy stopped 20 shots in his 600th career game, and the Tampa Bay Lightning won for the first time this season by topping the visiting Washington Capitals 3-1 on Saturday night.
Jake Guentzel had a goal and an assist, and Charle-Edouard D'Astous and Conor Geekie also found the net as Tampa Bay evened its record through two matches. Brandon Hagel had two assists.
Justin Sourdif scored for the Capitals, who lost the second part of their weekend back-to-back set.
Goaltender Charlie Lindgren made 27 saves for Washington, and teammate Dylan Strome skated in his 600th game.
After losing 5-1 at the New York Rangers on Thursday in their season opener, the Lightning needed less than 2 1/2 minutes to strike for their initial home goal. D'Astous sent in a shot near the right circle that beat Lindgren for the defenseman's first tally.
While Tampa Bay's power play went 0-for-7 in the opening defeat, it clicked early on the match's first man advantage when Sourdif went off for holding at 8:35. Though it did not find the net, the unit put plenty of pressure on Lindgren and had close chances.
As D'Astous did, Geekie ripped a shot that smoked Lindgren high on the left side to increase the lead to two goals at 16:30 as the club dominated by leading 14-5 in shots in the first period.
Following a 5-2 win at the defending Stanley Cup champion Carolina Hurricanes on Friday, the Capitals found their footing in the second, answered with a goal and matched Tampa Bay with seven shots.
Sourdif trimmed Washington's deficit in half at 7:04 after a turnover in the neutral zone. He raced toward the net and chipped in Jakob Chychrun's pass from the blue line for his first goal.
The teams skated 4-on-4 early in the third after Tom Wilson and Zemgus Girgensons roughed each other behind Vasilevskiy, but the Lightning had a crucial penalty kill in the middle portion to help preserve the lead.
With the net empty and just over two minutes remaining, Guentzel took a pass from Nikita Kucherov and iced the win.
--Field Level Media

items.title: Leon Draisaitl's deciding goal lifts Oilers past Kraken
items.author: Field Level Media
items.creator: Field Level Media
items.summary: Leon Draisaitl scored the tiebreaking goal with 2:27 remaining to give the Edmonton Oilers a 3-1 victory against the visiting Seattle Kraken on Saturday.
items.body:
Leon Draisaitl scored the tiebreaking goal with 2:27 remaining to give the Edmonton Oilers a 3-1 victory against the visiting Seattle Kraken on Saturday.
Connor McDavid added an empty-net goal with 1:05 left to clinch the victory.
Owen Michaels also scored for the Oilers and goaltender Devon Levi made 19 saves as the Oilers won their second straight after a season-opening 6-5 overtime loss to visiting Vancouver.
Bobby McMann tallied for the Kraken and Philipp Grubauer stopped 22 of 24 shots.
The deciding goal came after McDavid sent a pass back to defenseman Ryan Shea at the left point. Shea, with his back to the net, banked the puck high off the boards to keep it in the offensive zone. The puck floated through the slot untouched until it reached Draisaitl outside the top right edge of the crease and he quickly put it past Grubauer.
The Oilers took a 1-0 lead in the first period while outshooting the Kraken 10-5. Alex Formenton forced a turnover along the boards in the Seattle end and fed a backhanded pass to Michaels deep on the left wing. The rookie lifted a one-timer over Grubauer's shoulder and into the near upper corner of the net at 2:51. It was Michaels' second goal in as many games after also tallying in Thursday's 9-7 victory at Vancouver.
Seattle tied it with a power-play goal in the second, when it had an 11-4 edge in shots. Jordan Eberle got the puck behind the Edmonton net and fed McMann in the lower inside corner of the left faceoff circle. McMann put a shot into the near upper corner of the net, beating Levi at 9:06.
The Oilers, who led the NHL on the power play last season by converting 30.6% of their attempts, were held scoreless on three attempts with the man advantage by the Kraken, who were 31st of 32 teams last season on the penalty kill at 72.2%.
Edmonton remained without four of its top seven forwards with Ryan Nugent-Hopkins (lower body), Jason Dickinson (undisclosed), Zach Hyman (undisclosed) and Matt Savoie (undisclosed) all injured.
Forward Mackie Samoskevich made his Kraken debut after being activated off injured reserve (upper body) earlier in the day, with fellow forward Jacob Melanson going on the IR with an upper-body injury suffered in the season opener, a 6-1 victory Thursday at Calgary.
--Field Level Media

items.title: USA/MIDTERMS-Trump tente de mobiliser les électeurs dans l'Ohio
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Le président américain Donald Trump a adopté un ton combatif lors d'un rassemblement organisé samedi dans l'Ohio, l'un des Etats où le scrutin pour remporter un siège au Sénat lors des élections de mi-mandat pourrait être décisif.
items.body:
Le président américain Donald Trump a adopté un ton combatif lors d'un rassemblement organisé samedi dans l'Ohio, l'un des Etats où le scrutin pour remporter un siège au Sénat lors des élections de mi-mandat pourrait être décisif.
"Allez simplement voter", a dit le président républicain lors d'un rassemblement en soutien aux candidats de son parti aux postes de sénateur, Jon Husted, et de gouverneur, Vivek Ramaswamy.
"Si vous y allez, on va gagner, on va remporter une large victoire, et on va leur en faire voir de toutes les couleurs."
De nombreux sénateurs républicains sortants à travers le pays sont confrontés à de rudes vents contraires sur le plan politique, alors que la popularité de Donald Trump a chuté ces derniers mois en raison de l'augmentation du coût de la vie et de la guerre en Iran.
Les sondages suggèrent que les démocrates pourraient gagner du terrain lors des élections du 3 novembre, mais Donald Trump a affirmé que les républicains feraient mieux que ne le prévoient leurs détracteurs.
"Je pense que nous allons leur réserver une grosse surprise, car ils ne savent pas ce qu'il se passe", a-t-il déclaré à la foule rassemblée à Vandalia, dans l'Ohio.
Le sénateur républicain Jon Husted, nommé à ce siège en 2025 après la démission de J.D. Vance devenu vice-président, fait face à l'ancien sénateur démocrate Sherrod Brown, qui espère que les électeurs de l'Ohio se souviendront de son long parcours marqué par un populisme économique assumé alors qu'il tente de retrouver son siège.
Donald Trump a recueilli plus de 55% des voix dans l'Ohio lors de l'élection présidentielle de 2024.
L'Ohio fait partie des Etats où le [USN:L8N4500SK TEXT:"scrutin"] est considéré comme véritablement compétitifs pour remporter un siège au Sénat.
Voir aussi: LE POINT sur les élections de mi-mandat du 3 novembre aux Etats-Unis ([USN:L8N4560J1 TEXT:"Full Story"])

items.title: Cornell president vows 'serious look' at fraternities, sororities in wake of rape allegations
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Cornell University will examine the role of fraternities and sororities on campus following an outcry over the school's handling of a student's rape allegations, the Ivy League school's president said on Saturday.
items.body:
Cornell University will examine the role of fraternities and sororities on campus following an outcry over the school's handling of a student's rape allegations, the Ivy League school's president said on Saturday.
A [USN:L1N45O0OO TEXT:"civil lawsuit"] filed last month by the woman, who alleges she was drugged and raped in 2024 by several members of the Chi Phi fraternity, has sparked [USN:L6N45O0CP TEXT:"outrage and soul-searching"] at Cornell over its campus culture at the school in Ithaca, New York.
In a video message, Cornell University President Michael Kotlikoff said the school would take steps to prevent a similar situation in the future. That includes "a serious look at the role of fraternities and sororities in campus life," Kotlikoff said.
"At their best, these organizations can provide students with friendship, belonging, mentorship and a powerful sense of community," he said. "But being part of a group can never diminish individual responsibility."
The university will seek input, he said, from students, alumni and others on how to "preserve what is valuable about Greek life while strengthening individual accountability, transparency and a culture in which every member understands their responsibility to protect the safety and well-being of others."
The lawsuit against Cornell, seven fraternity members and others, alleges that the school failed to adequately punish some of the accused students.
The accused men have denied all wrongdoing, the New York Times reported.
Cornell has defended its handling of the matter, saying it launched a comprehensive investigation and barred the Chi Phi fraternity from campus. The school said it imposed a range of disciplinary measures, including expulsions.
But "we must do better," Kotlikoff said. "We don’t have all the answers, but we are committed to investigating and finding the answers our community deserves."
He vowed that university officials would "be more transparent" about their actions related to the 2024 incident, but he did not detail specific initiatives that the university would take.
"In the coming weeks, we will create additional opportunities for members of our community to ask questions and hear directly from university leadership," he said.
The case has reignited scrutiny of how law enforcement and universities handle sexual assault complaints, with students questioning whether processes are enough to protect them. It has also drawn the attention of New York state officials, who have appointed a special prosecutor to investigate.

items.title: Jiri Kulich's third-period goal lifts Sabres past winless Blackhawks
items.author: Field Level Media
items.creator: Field Level Media
items.summary: After missing most of last season with a blood clot, Jiri Kulich scored the game-winning goal with 6:40 remaining in regulation to propel the Buffalo Sabres to a 4-3 victory in their home opener over the Chicago Blackhawks on Saturday.
items.body:
After missing most of last season with a blood clot, Jiri Kulich scored the game-winning goal with 6:40 remaining in regulation to propel the Buffalo Sabres to a 4-3 victory in their home opener over the Chicago Blackhawks on Saturday.
Tage Thompson tallied a goal and an assist, and Jack Quinn and Rasmus Dahlin also scored for the Sabres, while Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen made 12 saves in the victory.
Ryan Donato, Tyler Bertuzzi and Oliver Moore scored for the Blackhawks.
Anton Frondell and Alex Vlasic finished with two assists apiece, while Spencer Knight stopped 24 of the 28 shots he faced as Chicago opened its season with three straight losses.
Donato started the scoring just under eight minutes into the game as he took a pass from Vlasic and fired a shot past Luukkonen to give the Blackhawks the early lead.
Chicago doubled the lead with 8:36 left in the first period after Frondell slid a cross-crease pass to Bertuzzi, who tapped it into the open net.
Quinn deked past a defender and then found Dahlin for a one-timer opportunity, but Knight kicked out the pad to deny the attempt with just over five minutes remaining in the first.
Quinn got another chance minutes later as he burned past a defending player and unloaded a powerful wrist shot that found the back of the net with 16:24 gone in the period.
Thompson knotted the game with his first goal of the young season as he tipped Louis Crevier's point shot past Knight with 14:19 left in the second.
Frank Nazar went on a short-handed breakaway with just over three minutes remaining in the middle frame, but Luukkonen got just enough of Nazar's five-hole shot to force it wide of the net.
Seconds after the penalty expired, Moore stepped out of the box, took a pass from Frondell and snuck it past Luukkonen to give the Blackhawks the 3-2 advantage with 18:18 expired in the period.
Peyton Krebs led the counterattack into the Blackhawks' end and sent a pass to Dahlin, who quickly wired it past Knight to knot up the contest at three apiece with 13:50 left in the third period.
Quinn looked to build upon his impressive night as he stormed toward the Blackhawks' net with 11:46 left, but Knight shut the door on the young speedster.
Kulich notched his first goal of the season for the 4-3 edge on assists from Owen Power and Thompson.
--Field Level Media

items.title: Ｆ１＝バーレーンＧＰ予選、フェルスタッペンが今季初ＰＰ
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［３日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
［３日　ロイター］ - 自動車レースＦ１の第１６戦、バーレーン・グランプリ（ＧＰ）は３日、マレーシアのセパンで予選を行い、個人総合優勝４回を誇るマックス・フェルスタッペン（オランダ、レッドブル）が今季自身初のポールポジション（ＰＰ）を獲得した。

フェルスタッペンは１分３５秒１３０をマーク。２番手のルイス・ハミルトン（英国、フェラーリ）を０秒２９８上回った。フェルスタッペンの同僚、アイザック・ハジャー（フランス）が３番手に入ったが、パワーユニットのコンポーネント交換で、決勝では５グリッド降格のペナルティーを受ける。

総合首位のキミ・アントネッリ（イタリア、メルセデス）は４番手でシャルル・ルクレール（モナコ、フェラーリ）が５番手。ランド・ノリス（英国）が６番手、オスカー・ピアストリ（オーストラリア）が７番手とマクラーレン勢が続き、総合２位のジョージ・ラッセル（英国、メルセデス）は８番手に終わった。

中東情勢を受けて、今大会はマレーシアで開催されている。

items.title: Australia's Treasurer heads to Japan for inaugural finance ministerial forum
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Australian Treasurer Jim Chalmers said he will travel to Japan on Sunday for talks with his Japanese counterpart in the first of an annual forum aiming to bolster bilateral ties.
items.body:
Australian Treasurer Jim Chalmers said he will travel to Japan on Sunday for talks with his Japanese counterpart in the first of an annual forum aiming to bolster bilateral ties.
The main purpose of the inaugural Australia-Japan Finance Ministerial Dialogue would be to discuss "investment opportunities, strategic financing and international engagement more broadly", Chalmers said in a statement.
He would seek to progress a deal with Japan's finance minister, Satsuki Katayama, to boost investment cooperation, the statement said.
Japan was Australia's fourth-largest foreign investor in 2024, with total investments valued at A$282.9 billion ($196.7 billion), according to the government.
The two countries face "many similar challenges as a result of global uncertainty, whether it’s higher energy prices driving up inflation or higher bond yields that are putting pressure on our budgets", the treasurer added.
While in Japan, Chalmers said he would also meet more than 30 CEOs and business leaders to showcase Australia as a "premier investment destination".
($1 = 1.4382 Australian dollars)

India and Pakistan summoned each other's top diplomats on Saturday (Oct 3) over a border incident on Friday, with New Delhi rejecting Islamabad's allegation that Indian forces had killed two unarmed Pakistani civilians and saying those involved had crossed illegally into Indian territory.

Pakistan's foreign ministry said earlier on Saturday that personnel from India's Border Security Force had used "unprovoked lethal force" against two unarmed Pakistani civilians in the Bedian sector along the international border on Friday.

"Pakistan categorically rejects any attempt to mischaracterize the deceased as 'infiltrators'," the ministry said in a statement.

Pakistan said it had summoned India's chargé d'affaires to lodge a protest over the incident and called for an "immediate, transparent and credible investigation".

India's foreign ministry later rejected what it called "baseless and motivated allegations" and said it had summoned the chargé d'affaires of the Pakistan High Commission to protest at the "continued facilitation of illegal cross-border infiltration from Pakistan".

The ministry said three people had crossed into Indian territory in the Ferozepur sector of Punjab and continued moving towards the border fence despite multiple warnings from the BSF to return to Pakistan.

"The BSF was compelled to engage them for posing an imminent security threat," the ministry said.

India said the incident reflected "a clear pattern of repeated cross-border movement by armed narcotics syndicates operating from Pakistan" and urged Islamabad to investigate what it described as cross-border infiltration and drug-smuggling activities.

India also urged Pakistan to respect the international border, observe bilateral arrangements and ensure its forces prevented unauthorised movement from its side.

Relations between the two nuclear-armed rivals have been strained since a four-day war in 2025, the worst in decades, followed by a militant attack on tourists in Indian Kashmir that killed 26 people.

New Delhi accused Pakistan of backing the attack, which Islamabad denied.

items.title: イエメン軍、首都サヌアでフーシ派に空爆実施
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: [４日 ロイター] - イエメン軍は４日未明、首都サヌアと北西部サアダで、親イラン武装組織フーシ派
items.body:
[４日 ロイター] - イエメン軍は４日未明、首都サヌアと北西部サアダで、親イラン武装組織フーシ派 に対して攻撃を実施していると明らかにした

軍の報道官によると、同軍は「重要目標」と称する標的を攻撃したが、詳細には触れなかった。

フーシ派系のアルマシラＴＶはこれに先立ち、サウジアラビアによるサヌアへの攻撃があったと伝えた。サウジ側からの確認は直ちには得られていない。

イランが支援するフーシ派とサウジが支援する政府軍との紛争は、２０２２年の停戦後ほぼ沈静化していたが、イラン戦争の余波で戦闘が再燃している。

フーシ派は７月にサウジに対する海上封鎖を宣言し、サウジ領土や船舶への攻撃を開始。また、イエメンの紅海沿岸で大幅に勢力域を拡大した。サウジはイエメン政府軍を支援し、同国内のフーシ派拠点に空爆を実施している。

items.title: Drew Rasmussen dominates, Rays stifle Yankees to win ALDS opener
items.author: Field Level Media
items.creator: Field Level Media
items.summary: Drew Rasmussen did not allow a hit through 7 2/3 scoreless innings and Jonathan Aranda belted a solo homer, lifting the Tampa Bay Rays to a 1-0 victory over the New York Yankees on Saturday in Game 1 of the American League Division Series in St. Petersburg, Fla.
items.body:
Drew Rasmussen did not allow a hit through 7 2/3 scoreless innings and Jonathan Aranda belted a solo homer, lifting the Tampa Bay Rays to a 1-0 victory over the New York Yankees on Saturday in Game 1 of the American League Division Series in St. Petersburg, Fla.
"In all honesty, my heartbeat was about a thousand beats per minute, so I just let (catcher) Liam (Hicks) call the game and just try to execute the pitches he called," Rasmussen said on the TNT Sports broadcast.
Austin Wells broke up Rasmussen's no-hit bid in the eighth with a blast down the right field line. However, he was thrown out in his attempt to stretch a double into a triple to end the inning.
"Obviously not a good decision there," Yankees manager Aaron Boone said. "Not sure if he saw something on his way between first and second that caused him to go there, but obviously a mistake there."
Wells said after he passed second base, he saw third base coach Luis Rojas with his hands up for him to stop there, but he already was committed to run to third.
"(They) made two good throws and it got me," Wells said. "Thought it kicked off more than it did, (right fielder Victor Mesa Jr.) made a good play on the ball. Two outs there, trying to make something happen, be aggressive with not much going on in the game. Obviously, love to safe there or standing on second base."
That was the lone hit allowed by Rasmussen (1-0), who struck out 10 batters in eight innings.
Right-hander Bryan Baker struck out two batters in a 1-2-3 ninth inning to secure his first career postseason save.
Aranda belted a solo homer in the third inning as one of the five hits for the Rays, who secured a 1-0 lead in the best-of-five series. Game 2 is Monday in St. Petersburg.
Aranda deposited a 2-2 changeup from right-hander Gerrit Cole (0-1) over the wall in right-center field to account for the scoring in the third inning.
The Yankees' bats went silent after outscoring the rival Boston Red Sox by an 18-2 margin and out-hitting them 26-7 during a two-game sweep in the wild-card round.
Captain Aaron Judge was left off New York's roster for the ALDS. Judge, 34, has not played since Sept. 16 due to a strained right calf. The three-time AL MVP landed on the injured list three days later and missed the Yankees' wild-card sweep earlier this week.
Rasmussen also dominated the Yankees in three of four meetings during the regular season, including a one-run, one-hit, 11-strikeout performance over 6 2/3 innings of a 6-1 romp on Sept. 22. The Rays clinched the AL East title with that victory.
"At that point, we had the opportunity to win the division. Obviously, this one is a postseason game. Both meaningful, both impactful," Rasmussen told reporters about his last two outings against New York.
Rasmussen allowed only a pair of walks, one each in the second and third innings, and retired the final 16 batters he faced on Saturday.
"It seemed like he went and doubled down tonight," Rays manager Kevin Cash said, noting Rasmussen's previous start against the Yankees. "Made it easy to sit back and just take some decisions out of our hands."
Rasmussen also showed his defensive chops by getting off the mound to field a bunt and throw out Ryan McMahon to begin the sixth inning. He finished that inning unscathed, marking the deepest no-hit bid in franchise history and the deepest into a postseason game the Yankees have ever been no-hit.
Cole permitted one run on five hits in five innings.
"Biggest issue is Rasmussen shutting us down," Boone said. "Obviously, we had a handful of guys hit some balls on the screws - Austin (Wells) being one of them a couple times there -- we just didn't generate enough, obviously."
--Field Level Media

items.title: Poor start for Red Wings can be turned around against Jets
items.author: Field Level Media
items.creator: Field Level Media
items.summary: The Detroit Red Wings' season opener couldn't have gone much worse. They'll look for a better result and more fan support when they host the Winnipeg Jets on Sunday afternoon.
items.body:
The Detroit Red Wings' season opener couldn't have gone much worse. They'll look for a better result and more fan support when they host the Winnipeg Jets on Sunday afternoon.
Detroit endured a tumultuous offseason in which former captain Dylan Larkin requested a trade and former top executive and franchise legend Steve Yzerman was reassigned to an advisory role.
Team owner Chris Ilitch still hasn't hired a permanent replacement for Yzerman, as in-house candidate Shawn Horcoff was named interim general manager prior to training camp. Restricted free agent Simon Edvinsson, one of the team's top defensemen, remains unsigned and returned to his native Sweden earlier in the week as negotiations stalled.
Larkin remains on the roster but missed Friday's opener against the New York Rangers with an upper-body injury and won't play on Sunday. He was heavily booed during pregame introductions and chants of "Sell the team," directed at Ilitch, cascaded from the stands at times during Detroit's 2-0 loss.
"Obviously he has to live with the ramifications of asking for a trade," coach Todd McLellan said of Larkin. "It's not comfortable for anybody and I feel bad for him, I do."
The rest of the players also had to deal with the vitriol from disenchanted fans.
"Everyone has a right to express their feelings and we just have to deal with it," defenseman Moritz Seider said after Friday's loss. "We handled it pretty well. Everyone gave it their best shot, and that's what we'll continue to do. You should be professional enough. We get paid to do our job. We have a great opportunity in front of us, to get back to work (Saturday) and prepare ourselves for hopefully our first win in two days."
The Red Wings' defense played well without Edvinsson but the offense was punchless without Larkin.
"We're going to have to score goals to win games," McLellan said. "The players that we have here, they have to understand and expect it from themselves and their teammates. You just can't rely on three or four guys."
The Jets opened their season on Friday with a 4-3 overtime loss to Boston. Winnipeg failed to protect a late 3-2 lead.
"I like a lot of what we did. There's mistakes, but we came out strong," said Kyle Connor, who extended his NHL record by scoring in a ninth straight season opener. "We had a little bit of a dip there, and obviously they got one to tie it up. But overall, I thought we played pretty quick."
The Jets have a major controversy of their own involving one of their top players. Star goaltender Connor Hellebuyck wants to be traded and didn't report to camp, prompting a suspension. Hellebuyck, like Larkin, is a Michigan native.
Stuart Skinner was the starting goaltender on Friday, making 26 saves. Skinner was signed to a two-year deal in July.
"I think we were ready. You saw us in the first ten minutes. I think the shots were like eight to one. We were ready to rock and roll. That's just kind of how the game works. There's ebbs and flows of the game," Skinner said. "You know, Boston's definitely going to have their push. We knew that was going to happen. But all in all, I thought we did a really good job and just got to tighten up a few things."
--Field Level Media

items.title: ＭＬＢ＝ヤンキース主将ジャッジ、地区シリーズはロースター外
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［３日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
［３日　ロイター］ - 米大リーグ（ＭＬＢ）ヤンキースが３日、レイズとの地区シリーズ（５回戦制）の２６人のロースターを発表。主将アーロン・ジャッジ外野手（３４）はメンバーを外れた。

ジャッジは右ふくらはぎの肉離れの影響で９月１６日以降プレーしておらず、その３日後に負傷者リスト（ＩＬ）入り。通算３回のア・リーグＭＶＰ（最優秀選手）選出を誇る同選手は、レッドソックスとのワイルドカードシリーズも欠場した。ヤンキースは同シリーズで２連勝し、地区シリーズに勝ち上がった。

ヤンキースのアーロン・ブーン監督は、ジャッジをロースターに入れなかったことについて「最終的にそれが最善と判断した」とコメント。「彼が復帰に近付いているように感じている」としながらも、「アーロンが本来の状態で復帰し、われわれがワールドシリーズで優勝するためには、あと１週間、彼が復帰に向けて努力を続けることが重要だ」と話した。

さらに同監督は「彼はランニングを始めたばかりで、打撃練習は数日前に再開した。これをさらに数日続けて、持久力を身に付けることが大事」とも述べた。

ジャッジは肋骨の骨折で３カ月以上離脱。９月８日に復帰した後、７試合に出場したが、打率１割７分４厘、１本塁打、３打点とふるわなかった。レギュラーシーズンでは６６試合に出場し、打率２割４分１厘、１８本塁打、４１打点だった。

items.title: サッカー＝欧州ＮＬ、イングランド7得点で大勝　スペイン3連勝
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［３日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
［３日　ロイター］ - サッカーの欧州ネーションズリーグ（ＮＬ）は３日、各地で１次リーグの試合を行い、リーグＡの３組ではイングランドが主将のハリー・ケーンらのゴールでクロアチアに７─０と大勝した。

イングランドは前半８分、ジュード・ベリンガムのパスを受けたケーンが守備陣２枚の間を抜けて先制ゴール。同２１分にベリンガムが決めて加点すると、３─０として迎えた同４５分にベリンガムのクロスからブカヨ・サカがネットを揺らした。

イングランドは後半もケーンとサカのゴールでリードを広げると、同４２分にベリンガムのお膳立てからモーガン・ロジャースにも得点が生まれた。ベリンガムは１試合１ゴール３アシスト。代表通算ゴール数を８９としたケーンは、これが１２４試合目。ピーター・シルトン氏の同代表最多出場記録まであと１試合となった。

同組のスペインはチェコを３─１で破り、開幕から３戦全勝とした。前半６分にラミン・ヤマルがペナルティーエリアの端から左足で強烈なシュートを放つと、同３５分には代表で２年以上ゴールのなかったロドリが決めて２点を先行。後半に１点を失ったが、最後はミケル・メリノのゴールで突き放した。

これにより、同組ではスペインが勝ち点９で首位、イングランドは同６で２位としている。

リーグＢの１組ではスイスがスロベニアを２─１で下して３戦全勝で首位をキープ。スコットランドは北マケドニアを２─０で破り、スロベニアと同じ勝ち点４とした。

items.title: アジア大会＝日本選手団、金メダル83個で60年ぶりに最多更新
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［３日　ロイター］　 -
items.body:
［３日　ロイター］　 - 愛知・名古屋アジア大会では３日、日本選手団の金メダル数が８３個に到達。これまでの記録を上回り、最多となった。１９６６年バンコク大会で記録した７８を６０年ぶりに更新した。

日本はソフトボール決勝では中国に７─０で快勝し、７連覇を達成。柔道混合団体ではカザフスタンを４─０で下し、３連覇を果たした。ラグビー７人制女子決勝では中国に１０─５で勝利し、８年ぶりの金メダル。水球男子でも優勝した。

セパタクロー男子クワッド（４人制）では日本初の金メダルに輝き、ブレイキン男子では半井重幸（ダンサー名・SHIGEKIX）が２連覇を達成。初採用のパデル、女子ダブルスは塚本早紀、徳本佳恵組が制した。

テニスの混合ダブルスでは柴原瑛菜、フレンド原ジェイ組が青山修子、楠原悠介組をストレートで下して優勝。同大会のテニス競技の決勝が日本人対決となったのは今回が初めてだった。

サッカー男子決勝では日本が韓国に０─１で敗戦。バレーボール男子決勝で、日本はイランにセットカウント１─３で負けた。

日本は今大会、３日の競技を終えた時点で銀メダルは９５個で銅メダルは９１個。金メダルと合わせて２６９個と、３４１個の中国に次ぐ２位のメダル数を記録している。

items.title: PGA club pro Michael Block takes 1-stroke lead after 36 holes in Allentown
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Michael Block needed only 30 shots on the back nine and posted a bogey-free 7-under 63 on Saturday to take a one-stroke lead after two rounds of the inaugural Jefferson Lehigh Valley Classic in Allentown, Pa.
items.body:
Michael Block needed only 30 shots on the back nine and posted a bogey-free 7-under 63 on Saturday to take a one-stroke lead after two rounds of the inaugural Jefferson Lehigh Valley Classic in Allentown, Pa.
Block, a 50-year-old PGA Tour Champions rookie, stands at 11 under through 36 holes. That puts him one ahead of New Zealand's Steven Alker and two ahead of first-round co-leader Richard Green of Australia.
Block, who continues to serve as the head golf professional at Arroyo Trabuco Golf Club in Mission Viejo, Calif., gained a following with a tie for 15th place at the 2023 PGA Championship.
Block, who shot a 4-under par 66 on Friday, opened with back-to-back birdies on Saturday. He parred the last seven holes on the front nine, then birdied five of the first seven holes coming in.
He is highly appreciative of the welcome he has received on the tour.
"So the support I have from the fellow Champions Tour players is amazing," Block said. "The relationships I've gotten in six events/seven, is crazy, and I really appreciate those guys. These guys have been living the Tour life, the PGA Tour life and Champions Tour life for, you know, 20-30 years, and I'm just out here -- and they know my scenario. I'm out here as a club pro, and being out here for my seventh event in my life, and they really support me, which is really cool. Trust me, it helps a lot."
In Block's fifth Champions start at The Ally Challenge five weeks ago, he also held the lead after 36 holes. But he was passed by Alker during the final round and ended up tied for third.
What did Block learn from that experience?
"Yeah, from Ally, just keep being you," he said. "Like, don't try to be the quiet Michael. Quiet Michael doesn't work. Michael having fun works. Michael being quiet, Michael trying to be somebody he's not doesn't work. That's what I'm going to do tomorrow."
In contrast to Block, who's happy just to be on the verge of qualifying for the Charles Schwab Cup playoffs, Alker has won three times in 2026, owns 13 PGA Tour Champions titles and ranks No. 3 on the Schwab Cup money list.
The 55-year-old has posted matching 65s and, like Block, played bogey-free golf on Saturday. He shot 31 on the inward half and played the par-3's in 2-under.
Alker is well aware the gallery will be flocking to Block on Sunday.
"He's got a great following and I think the crowds will be good tomorrow and want him to do well," Alker said. "He's a bit different, he likes to talk about things. It's fun. I kind of like watching him play a little bit, see how he goes about the game. Not that I'll take a whole lot of it forward, but I just like watching him play and how he goes about his game.
"He's got game, I've got to bring it tomorrow."
Ryan Armour fired a 64 to move into fourth at 8-under. Tag Ridings (65), South Korea's Y.E. Yang (69) and Sweden's Robert Karlsson (69) share fifth at 7-under. Yang and Karlsson joined Green atop the leaderboard after the first round.
--Field Level Media

items.title: México dice que investigación de la FDA sobre la lechuga no identificó la fuente de la contaminación
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary:
El Ministerio de Salud de México dijo el sábado que la investigación de la Administración de Alimentos y Medicamentos de EEUU (FDA por su sigla en inglés
) sobre el brote del parásito Cyclospora, relacionado con la lechuga iceberg troceada de Taylor Farms en México, no identificó de forma concluyente el origen de la contaminación.
items.body:
El Ministerio de Salud de México dijo el sábado que la investigación de la Administración de Alimentos y Medicamentos de EEUU (FDA por su sigla en inglés
) sobre el brote del parásito Cyclospora, relacionado con la lechuga iceberg troceada de Taylor Farms en México, no identificó de forma concluyente el origen de la contaminación.
La Cofepris, el organismo regulador de la seguridad alimentaria de México, señaló que los análisis realizados por su laboratorio nacional de referencia en materias primas, productos terminados y agua de las instalaciones investigadas en relación con el brote dieron negativo para el parásito Cyclospora.
El regulador añadió que los resultados ambientales por sí solos no constituyen una prueba concluyente de que los productos agrícolas fueran la fuente de la contaminación.
La FDA [USN:L6N45O12Z TEXT:"declaró el viernes"] que había encontrado un fuerte vínculo epidemiológico y de trazabilidad entre el brote y la lechuga iceberg troceada retirada del mercado, producida por Taylor Farms en México, pero señaló que no había pruebas suficientes para determinar cómo se produjo la contaminación.
La agencia informó de dos muestras ambientales positivas para Cyclospora en México: una procedente de las aguas residuales que salían de una planta de procesamiento y otra de una zanja de drenaje en una explotación de lechuga iceberg.
Los Centros para el Control y la Prevención de Enfermedades (CDC) declararon el fin del brote el 11 de septiembre. El brote afectó a 12.883 personas en 21 estados, provocó la hospitalización de 570 personas y se relacionó con dos fallecimientos.
México afirmó que había cooperado durante toda la investigación, proporcionando información sobre la trazabilidad, inspecciones y muestras, y que continuaría la cooperación técnica con las autoridades sanitarias estadounidenses.

items.body:
Home / World News / Strait of Hormuz will not reopen until conditions are met, says Iran

Strait of Hormuz will not reopen until conditions are met, says Iran Iran's parliament speaker Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf said the Strait of Hormuz will remain closed until Washington meets seven conditions agreed under a June interim pact

Photo: Bloomberg

Reuters DUBAI 1 min read Last Updated : Oct 04 2026 | 12:18 PM IST

Listen to This Article

The Strait of Hormuz will not reopen until seven Iranian conditions set out in a June interim agreement with the US are met, Nournews reported Iran's parliament speaker Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf as saying on Sunday, a few days after Tehran received Washington's reply to its diplomatic proposal.
  "The Americans, who say something different in the media, have recently put forward proposals through a mediator. But they must understand that the period of dragging out the process and dictating one-sided demands is over," Qalibaf was quoted as saying.
  "The position of the Islamic Republic of Iran is completely clear and firm, and the Strait of Hormuz will not be opened until our seven conditions, based on the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding, are met." 
 

(Only the headline and picture of this report may have been reworked by the Business Standard staff; the rest of the content is auto-generated from a syndicated feed.)

items.title: Mexico says FDA lettuce probe did not conclusively identify contamination source
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Mexico's Health Ministry said on Saturday that a US Food and Drug Administration investigation into the cyclospora parasite outbreak linked to shredded iceberg lettuce from Taylor Farms in Mexico did not conclusively identify the source of contamination.
items.body:
Mexico's Health Ministry said on Saturday that a US Food and Drug Administration investigation into the cyclospora parasite outbreak linked to shredded iceberg lettuce from Taylor Farms in Mexico did not conclusively identify the source of contamination.
Mexico's food-safety regulator Cofepris said tests conducted by its national reference laboratory on raw materials, finished products and water from the facility investigated in the outbreak were negative for the cyclospora parasite.
The regulator added that environmental findings alone do not constitute conclusive evidence that agricultural products were the source of contamination.
The FDA said [USN:L4N45O17K TEXT:"on Friday"] it found a strong epidemiological and traceback link between the outbreak and recalled shredded iceberg lettuce produced by Taylor Farms in Mexico, but said there was insufficient evidence to determine how contamination occurred.
The agency reported two environmental samples positive for cyclospora in Mexico, one from wastewater leaving a processing facility and another from a drainage ditch at an iceberg lettuce farm.
The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention declared the outbreak over on September 11. The outbreak sickened 12,883 people in 21 states, hospitalized 570 and was linked to two deaths.
Mexico said it cooperated throughout the investigation, providing traceability information, inspections and samples, and would continue technical cooperation with US health authorities.

items.title: Lula tem 46% dos votos válidos contra 45% de Flávio Bolsonaro no 1º turno, mostra Quaest
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: O presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) e o senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) estão em empate técnico nos votos válidos do primeiro turno da eleição presidencial de domingo, com vantagem numérica de 1 ponto percentual para o petista, mostrou pesquisa Quaest neste sábado.
items.body:
O presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) e o senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) estão em empate técnico nos votos válidos do primeiro turno da eleição presidencial de domingo, com vantagem numérica de 1 ponto percentual para o petista, mostrou pesquisa Quaest neste sábado.
Lula tem 46% dos votos válidos, quando são excluídos os brancos, nulos e indecisos, enquanto Flávio soma 45%. A margem de erro da pesquisa é de 2 pontos percentuais, para mais ou para menos.
Para vencer no primeiro turno no domingo, um candidato precisa ter mais de 50% dos votos válidos.
Nos chamados votos totais, o presidente aparece com 40% (eram 39% na pesquisa anterior), contra 38% do senador de oposição (eram 34%). Os indecisos somam 3% (eram 5% na pesquisa anterior), enquanto aqueles que dizem que votarão em branco, anularão o voto ou não votarão em nenhum candidato chegam a 10%, mesma parcela da pesquisa anterior.
Já num eventual segundo turno entre os dois, Flávio Bolsonaro aparece numericamente à frente, com 44% (eram 42%), enquanto Lula registra os mesmos 42% do último levantamento.

items.title: NC State RB Jayden Scott (foot) leaves game vs. Louisville
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Jayden "Duke" Scott, North Carolina State's top running back, left Saturday's home game against Louisville early with a lower-body injury.
items.body:
Jayden "Duke" Scott, North Carolina State's top running back, left Saturday's home game against Louisville early with a lower-body injury.
He was later seen on the sideline wearing a boot on his left foot.
Scott walked to the locker room after a Wolfpack drive in the first quarter.
In his third season in Raleigh, Scott had 346 yards and four touchdowns on 57 carries through the Wolfpack's first four games. He ran five times for 12 yards on Saturday.
With Scott out, Davion Gause received the majority of the carries for NC State (2-2, 0-1 Atlantic Coast Conference) through the first three quarters.
--Field Level Media

items.title: Reports: Pitt QB Mason Heintschel (knee) done for season
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Pitt quarterback Mason Heintschel will reportedly miss the rest of the season with a torn anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee, multiple outlets reported Saturday.
items.body:
Pitt quarterback Mason Heintschel will reportedly miss the rest of the season with a torn anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee, multiple outlets reported Saturday.
According to ESPN, Heintschel suffered the injury during Friday night's 35-33 road victory over Virginia Tech. he was scrambling in the third quarter when he took a hit to the knee while being tackled by two Virginia Tech players.
The sophomore has passed for 1,304 yards and 14 touchdowns against one interception this season while leading Pitt to its second 5-0 start since 1991.
Holden Geriner, a fifth-year quarterback, replaced Heintschel against the Hokies and is the likely starting quarterback when the Panthers host North Carolina on Oct. 10.
Heintschel completed 10 of 18 passes for 113 yards and a touchdown before exiting. Geriner went 8 of 12 for 78 yards and one score.
Geriner played previously for Auburn (2022-24) and Texas State (2025). He has completed 19 of 26 passes for 219 yards and two touchdowns this season.
--Field Level Media

items.title: Top 25 roundup: No. 25 Mizzou runs it up in rout of No. 8 Florida
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Austin Simmons threw for 340 yards and two touchdowns, Jamal Roberts ran for 211 yards and three scores, and No. 25 Missouri's defense shut down star running back Jadan Baugh in a 45-17 victory Saturday afternoon over No. 8 Florida in Columbia, Mo.
items.body:
Austin Simmons threw for 340 yards and two touchdowns, Jamal Roberts ran for 211 yards and three scores, and No. 25 Missouri's defense shut down star running back Jadan Baugh in a 45-17 victory Saturday afternoon over No. 8 Florida in Columbia, Mo.
Roberts broke two long second-half runs, one for 77 yards and later an 80-yard touchdown for the Tigers, who scored 35 straight points after the score was tied 10-10 late in the first half, scoring on six straight possessions. Mizzou coach Eli Drinkwitz improved to 2-10 against teams ranked in the Top 10 of the Associated Press poll.
Simmons hooked up with Donovan Olugbode on a 47-yard touchdown pass, and with Caleb Goodie Sr. on a 31-yard score in the second quarter. Cayden Lee led the Tigers (4-1, 1-1 Southeastern Conference), with 110 receiving yards on eight catches. Simmons finished 23-of-30 passing.
Baugh, a Heisman Trophy candidate after the first month of the season, gained only 13 rushing yards on 12 carries for the Gators (4-1, 2-1). He came in with 11 touchdowns to lead FBS, and had rushed for at least 100 yards in five straight games dating back to last season.
No. 2 Georgia 38, Vanderbilt 14
Gunner Stockton completed 25 of 32 passes for 295 yards and three touchdowns to help lead the Bulldogs to victory over the Commodores in Athens, Ga.
Stockton connected with 10 receivers, including Dwight Phillips Jr., who had five catches for 75 yards and a score. The Bulldogs (5-0, 3-0 SEC) have won all their games by at least 24 points. They outscored the Commodores 17-0 in the second half after going into halftime with a 21-14 lead.
Vanderbilt (3-2, 0-2) was without freshman quarterback Jared Curtis, who was scratched before the game with an undisclosed injury. In his place, Blaze Berlowitz completed 12 of 23 passes for 190 yards and a touchdown. Junior Sherrill posted seven receptions for 107 yards and a score for the Commodores, who dropped their second straight game.
No. 3 Notre Dame 37, North Carolina 26
CJ Carr threw for four touchdowns and ran for another as the Fighting Irish beat the Tar Heels in rainy conditions in Chapel Hill, N.C.
Jordan Faison caught two touchdown passes as part of an eight-catch, 132-yard receiving effort for Notre Dame (5-0). Carr completed 21 of 29 passes for 234 yards. Jonaz Walton rushed for 120 yards on 23 carries.
Billy Edwards Jr. threw for three touchdowns, two interceptions and 208 yards for North Carolina (2-2), which was held to 285 yards of total offense. Jordan Shipp had 109 receiving yards on seven catches.
No. 4 Miami 41, Clemson 13
Mark Fletcher Jr. ran for two touchdowns and Darian Mensah passed for a TD and ran for another to lead the Hurricanes in a rout of the host Tigers.
Miami (5-0, 3-0 Atlantic Coast Conference) moved into sole possession of first place in the league standings while beating Clemson (3-2, 2-1) on its home field for the first time since 2010. Fletcher finished with 77 yards on 16 carries. Mensah completed 18 of 27 passes for 227 yards.
The Hurricanes' defense recorded six sacks, including five in the first half, against Clemson quarterback Tait Reynolds. He completed 29 of 44 passes for 295 yards with no touchdowns and one interception, which resulted in a 39-yard pick-six by Miami's JJ Dunnigan to close the scoring.
No. 5 Ohio State 31, No. 14 Iowa 14
Jeremiah Smith set two more school records and strengthened his Heisman Trophy candidacy as the Buckeyes defeated the Hawkeyes in Iowa City.
Smith, a junior, made his 36th career touchdown catch in the third quarter to surpass Chris Olave's school record and give Ohio State a 24-6 lead. On Ohio State's next drive, Smith's 10th catch of the game was his 206th for the Buckeyes to move one ahead of former record-holder Emeka Egbuka. Smith finished with 11 catches for 206 yards.
Iowa finished with just 238 total yards and lost the turnover battle 2-0.
No. 6 Indiana 47, Rutgers 15
Josh Hoover was 20-for-27 passing for 251 yards and four touchdowns, Turbo Richard racked up a career-high 204 yards and a score on the ground and the Hoosiers thrashed the Scarlet Knights in Piscataway, N.J.
The Hoosiers (5-0, 2-0 Big Ten) extended the nation's longest winning streak to 21. Lee Beebe Jr. had a big second half to finish with 122 rushing yards and a touchdown, while Charlie Becker made eight catches for 107 yards and two TDs. Indiana became the first Big Ten team with two 100-yard rushers and two 100-yard receivers in one game since 1995.
Rutgers' AJ Surace relieved Dylan Lonergan at quarterback before halftime, with Lonergan apparently injured on a QB sneak attempt. Surace was the more effective passer for the Scarlet Knights (1-4, 0-2), with 128 yards and a 53-yard touchdown to Ben Black III.
No. 7 Alabama 56, No. 16 Mississippi State 23
Keelon Russell totaled four touchdowns, as the Crimson Tide rolled past the Bulldogs in an SEC clash in Starkville, Miss.
Russell threw for 285 yards and three touchdowns and ran for one more. Rico Scott had 56 receiving yards and two touchdowns for Alabama (5-0, 3-0 SEC), which is 5-0 for the first time in Kalen DeBoer's three seasons.
Mississippi State quarterback Kamario Taylor completed 19 of 34 passes for 258 yards, three touchdowns and two interceptions. The Bulldogs have lost 17 straight games against the Crimson Tide. Taylor went to the locker room with an undisclosed injury early in the fourth quarter, and reserve Parker Puckett finished the game under center.
No. 10 BYU 17, TCU 10
Quarterback Bear Bachmeier rushed for two touchdowns and Faletau Satuala recorded a key interception as the Cougars downed the Horned Frogs in Big 12 play at Fort Worth, Texas.
Bachmeier rushed for 66 yards on 15 carries and completed 11 of 24 passes for 62 yards for BYU (4-0, 2-0 Big 12), which has started 4-0 in three consecutive seasons for the first time in program history. Star running back LJ Martin carried the ball just twice for 16 yards before exiting in the first quarter with a right leg injury. The reigning Big 12 Offensive Player of the Year was ruled out at halftime.
Jaden Craig was 18-of-25 passing for 187 yards, one touchdown and one interception for TCU (2-3, 0-2). Kari Ashley had six receptions for 108 yards and one touchdown and Jeremy Payne had 100 yards from scrimmage (77 rushing, 23 receiving).
No. 11 LSU 63, McNeese 14
Sam Leavitt passed for three touchdowns in limited action, Corey Barber Jr. caught two of the scoring passes, Harlem Berry and Stacy Gage each rushed for more than 100 yards as the host Tigers thrashed the FCS-level Cowboys in Baton Rouge, La.
Leavitt, who has been hampered by a hamstring injury, did not run the ball and played just the first half before being relieved by Landen Clark with LSU (4-1) leading 35-0. Leavitt passed for 176 yards and an interception.
Barber, a freshman who had just one reception for 15 yards before Saturday, finished with seven catches for 83 yards and his first career TDs. Berry had the first 100-yard rushing game of his two-year career, finishing with 125 yards and a score, and Gage rushed for 110 yards and two TDs on six carries. The Tigers outgained McNeese (2-4) 731-196 and finished with a 37-6 advantage in first downs.
No. 12 Texas Tech 29, Colorado 7
John Curry intercepted a pass in the end zone for a touchdown, Brice Pollock had two interceptions and Malik Esquerra added another pick as the Red Raiders rallied for a victory over the Buffaloes in Boulder, Colo.
All three third-quarter Colorado (2-3, 0-2 Big 12) drives ended in interceptions as the Red Raiders (5-0, 2-0) overcame a 7-3 halftime deficit. As Curry rushed off the edge with 7:10 remaining in the game, he reached up and intercepted Colorado quarterback Isaac Wilson's pass in the end zone for a 22-7 lead.
Texas Tech's Will Hammond threw for 134 yards and a touchdown. J'Koby Williams rushed for 88 yards and Quinten Joyner ran in a score. Wilson was 26 of 44 for 290 yards with one touchdown and three interceptions. Joseph Williams caught 10 passes for 93 yards and a score and threw an interception on a trick play.
No. 17 Tennessee 24, Auburn 14
DeSean Bishop rushed for a career-high 220 yards and three second-half touchdowns to rally the Volunteers past the Tigers in the first matchup between these SEC foes since 2020 in Knoxville, Tenn.
The former walk-on from Knoxville carried 34 times while becoming the first Tennessee running back to go for 200 yards and three scores since Eric Gray in 2019. Tennessee coach Josh Heupel benched freshman quarterback Faizon Brandon late in the first half after he went 3-for-8 passing for no yards and one interception. Backup George MacIntyre completed 8 of 10 passes for 86 yards.
Auburn's Byrum Brown was 22-for-33 passing for 159 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions. He rushed for 107 yards on 19 attempts and scored the first touchdown for the Tigers, who built a 7-3 halftime lead.
No. 18 Southern California 25, Washington 21
The Trojans scored a pair of third-quarter touchdowns less than two minutes apart, then held firm on the Huskies' final drive to survive with a win in Los Angeles.
The Trojans (5-1, 2-1 Big Ten Conference) surrendered a pair of fourth-down conversions that allowed the Huskies (3-2, 0-2) to advance into the red zone with less than a minute remaining in regulation. USC's defense buckled down, however.
USC's Jayden Maiava finished with one of his more statistically muted efforts, going 21-of-34 passing for 245 yards with a touchdown and an interception. King Miller led the Trojans with 81 yards rushing. Demond Williams Jr. finished 15-of-26 passing for 198 yards and one touchdown and Brian Bonner rushed for 89 yards for Washington.
No. 20 Houston 27, UCF 17
Conner Weigman scored three times on the ground in the second half as the host Cougars shrugged off a ragged first 40 minutes and roared from behind to beat UCF.
Weigman's third rushing touchdown, a 1-yard plunge with 10:15 to play, gave Houston (4-1, 1-1 Big 12) its first lead. On the ensuing drive, Weigman -- who finished with 239 passing yards -- connected with Trent Walker for a 43-yard catch-and-run to set the table for Jonathan Dimas' 40-yard field goal with 4:14 to play.
Keyone Jenkins passed for 253 yards and a touchdown and ran for another score to lead UCF's (3-2, 1-1) attack. Josh Derry caught seven passes for 101 yards and one touchdown.
No. 21 SMU 25, Boston College 16
The host Mustangs carried a three-point lead into halftime and nearly pitched a second-half shutout in a win over the Eagles. Kevin Jennings threw touchdowns to Randy Pittman Jr. and Derrick McFall after intermission, finishing 20-for-30 passing for 160 yards.
SMU (4-1, 2-1 ACC) sacked Boston College quarterback Mason McKenzie five times and held the Eagles (2-3, 0-2) scoreless over seven straight possessions from the first quarter until a touchdown with 2:07 left in regulation. Marques White recorded three of the five sacks.
McKenzie also threw for two scores and 208 yards on a 20-of-31 passing day. He also led all ball carriers with 74 yards on 21 attempts. Evan Dickens and Danny Edgehill each caught one touchdown pass.
No. 22 Boise State 37, Utah State 18
Maddux Madsen passed for two touchdowns and Dylan Riley rushed for two scores as the Broncos ran away with a victory over the Aggies in the inaugural Pac-12 contest for both teams at Boise, Idaho.
Madsen completed 17 of 21 passes for 244 yards as the Broncos (4-1, 1-0 Pac-12) defeated Utah State for the 11th consecutive time and 23rd time in the past 24 meetings. Matt Wagner and Ben Ford caught touchdown passes for Boise State, which also saw Jake Ripp return an interception for a touchdown.
Javen Jacobs caught a touchdown pass and rushed for 139 yards on 10 carries, including gains of 64 and 46 yards for Utah State (1-4, 0-1). Eli Wood had seven receptions for 102 yards and a touchdown. Grady Brosterhous completed 12 of 18 passes for 129 yards and two touchdowns.
No. 24 Kentucky 35, South Carolina 34 (OT)
Kenny Minchey's two-point-conversion pass to Willie Rodriguez lifted the Wildcats to an overtime win over the Gamecocks in Columbia, S.C.
Minchey connected with Henry Boyer on a 6-yard touchdown to set up the successful two-point attempt and cap the largest road comeback in program history after Kentucky (4-1, 2-1 SEC) trailed 17-0 in the second quarter. Minchey had 272 passing yards and three touchdowns.
LaNorris Sellers threw for 226 yards and two touchdowns while rushing 17 times for 147 yards. Matt Fuller and Jabree Coleman each had a rushing touchdown, while Mazeo Bennett Jr. had 92 receiving yards, and DJ Black and Brown each caught a touchdown pass for South Carolina (2-3, 0-3).
--Field Level Media

items.title: Tarik Skubal pitches Dodgers past Braves in Game 1 of NLDS
items.author: Field Level Media
items.creator: Field Level Media
items.summary: LOS ANGELES -- Tarik Skubal dominated over six innings, three home runs powered the offense and the Los Angeles Dodgers opened the National League Division Series with a 5-3 victory over the Atlanta Braves on Saturday.
items.body:
LOS ANGELES -- Tarik Skubal dominated over six innings, three home runs powered the offense and the Los Angeles Dodgers opened the National League Division Series with a 5-3 victory over the Atlanta Braves on Saturday.
Teoscar Hernandez, Kyle Tucker and Max Muncy all went deep as the Dodgers started their quest to become the first National League club to win three consecutive championships and the first major league team to do it since the New York Yankees from 1998-2000.
Skubal (1-0) gave up one run on two hits with two walks and seven strikeouts in his first postseason start for Los Angeles after arriving in a trade-deadline deal from the Detroit Tigers.
Sean Murphy and Ozzie Albies hit home runs for the Braves, who entered off a wild-card round victory over the Philadelphia Phillies and are trying to advance past the NLDS for the first time since winning the World Series in 2021.
Left-hander Dylan Dodd opened the game with three scoreless innings for Atlanta before giving way to Victor Mederos (0-1), who gave up Hernandez's home run and recorded just one out in the fourth inning.
On a blisteringly hot day, with the temperature at 100 degrees to open the game, Skubal allowed only one hit through his first five scoreless innings on the mound.
Hernandez backed Skubal with a two-run home run in the fourth inning for a 2-0 advantage.
"I really don't care if I strike out in big situations. I always want to be the guy to be in those moments," Hernandez said. "I worked really hard for it, and I think the bigger the moment, the more focused I get. Just trying to put together a good at-bat for the team. Obviously if I get a good pitch to hit, I just try to put a good swing on it."
The Braves finally got to Skubal in the sixth when Murphy hit a home run to center to bring Atlanta to within a run.
The Dodgers increased their advantage in the bottom of the sixth against AJ Smith-Shawver when Tucker slugged a two-run home run and Muncy followed two batters later with a solo shot down the line in right field for a 5-1 advantage.
Tucker's contribution on offense came after a disappointing regular season when his .715 OPS was lower than all but one Dodgers player who played in at least 90 games. Tucker is in the first season of a four-year, $240 million contract.
Albies got the Braves within two runs in the ninth with a two-run home run off Tanner Scott. Evan Phillips entered the game with two outs and walked Mauricio Dubon to bring the tying run to the plate. But he earned the save by retiring Austin Riley on a groundout to short.
"I thought we put up some competitive at-bats. Really nice swing from Murphy right there and then and then not giving up," Riley said. "With Ozzie, the two-run homer, that was encouraging. Just ran out of time today."
--Doug Padilla, Field Level Media

items.body:
Home / Markets / IPO / Jio IPO likely by Oct end at enterprise valuation of above ₹12 trillion

Jio IPO likely by Oct end at enterprise valuation of above ₹12 trillion Jio Platforms IPO is touted as India's largest public offer at an estimated size of $3.8 billion

Jio Platforms had filed its draft IPO papers in June | Image: Bloomberg

Press Trust of India New Delhi 4 min read Last Updated : Oct 04 2026 | 11:41 AM IST

Listen to This Article

Digital services major Jio Platforms is likely to get listed by the end of this month at an enterprise valuation of $143-146 billion or above ₹12 trillion, sources tracking the development said.
Jio Platforms IPO is touted as India's largest public offer at an estimated size of $3.8 billion.
The company has concluded overseas roadshows and is expected to file final papers with market regulator SEBI for the initial public offering in the week starting October 12, banking and other sources who did not wish to be identified told PTI.
"Based on interest received from overseas roadshows, Jio Platforms is likely to list at a base enterprise valuation of $143-146 billion or at least ₹12 trillion by end of this month," one of the banking sources said.
 

An email sent to Jio Platforms (JPL) seeking comments based on available information did not elicit any reply.
Also Read

T-Mobile, Jio launch world's first 5G Standalone roaming connection
